(a) In General.—The last sentence of subsections (b) and (c) of section 1870 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395gg) are each amended—
        (1) by striking “third year” and inserting “fifth year”; and 
        (2) by striking “three-year” and inserting “five-year”.  
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendments made by subsection (a) shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to section 1870 of the Social Security Act, changing a three-year period to a five-year period, and sets an effective date. There is no tempting reading here: it provides for no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: The amendments made by subsection (a) shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This section only changes a time period in Medicare overpayment rules (section 1870 of the Social Security Act) from three years to five, and sets an effective date. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or new right for outside parties to challenge a federal decision. Linking it to administrative overpayment procedures is tempting, but changing a time limit is like the statute-of-limitations trap and is not participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends statutory language to change specific time periods from three years to five years. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, or consultation with outside entities. The changes are purely legislative adjustments to existing provisions without any participatory process described.
qwen_chat.s: (a) In General.—The last sentence of subsections (b) and (c) of section 1870 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395gg) are each amended— (1) by striking “third year” and inserting “fifth year”; and (2) by striking “three-year” and inserting “five-year”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the timeline for a program implies a consultation with stakeholders, but the text itself only describes a mechanical amendment to statutory language regarding time periods ("third year" to "fifth year"). There is no mention of any process involving outside parties, public comment, or advisory bodies.
